newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Darts match joins communities on divided Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Darts match joins communities on divided Cyprus.

text.p: Darts players will compete for charity in a medieval abbey in Cyprus on Sunday in a rare meeting of the estranged Greek and Turkish communities.
Local darts players have chosen the sport, widely popular on both sides of the island, to try to improve contacts between two communities separated by barbed wire since 1974.

Some 400 players will gather at the Bellapais abbey in Turkish-held north Cyprus on Sunday for the day-long tournament which will start with blood donations in aid of sufferers of thalassaemia, a hereditary blood disorder.
"It is a sporting event which will be non-political in aid of charity," said Greek Cypriot Tom Thoupos, one of the organisers.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when Turkish forces invaded the island's north in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia backed by the military junta ruling Greece.

Contact between the two communities remains limited to a smattering of professional groups meeting under United Nations auspices to discuss issues of mutual interest, while bi-communal relations have cooled significantly over the past year after a series of killings on the ceasefire line.

"We try to sponsor anything which gives Turkish and Greek Cypriots an opportunity to get together whether in the (U.N. controlled) buffer zone or on the respective sides," said Peter Schmitz, senior political adviser in the United Nations peacekeeping force stationed on the island.
